title: Point the tests at an in-memory test database
problem: The tests in test_messages.py use the production app, whose database file lives on a server path that doesn't exist here (as on a CI runner), so every request fails with 'unable to open database file'. Write the three fixtures in conftest.py: a fresh in-memory SQLite engine per test with the tables created, a Session for arranging and checking data, and a client for an app built on the test engine.
requirements: Edit only conftest.py. Don't change app.py or test_messages.py
engine: a new in-memory SQLite engine per test that works across threads (StaticPool and check_same_thread=False), with Base.metadata.create_all run on it, disposed after the test
db: a Session bound to the test engine, closed after the test
client: a TestClient (used as a context manager) for create_app(engine); never the module-level production app
contract: conftest.py defines fixtures engine() -> Engine, db(engine) -> Session and client(engine) -> TestClient
expectedBehavior: pytest -q shows 6 passed; every test starts with empty tables; rows the app commits are visible through db
edgeCases: A test that runs after another test inserted rows
Data arranged through db and then read by the app in another thread
A test that uses db without client
hints: Conceptual: an in-memory SQLite database exists only inside one connection. A second connection, for example one opened by another thread, sees a different, empty database. So the engine must hand out the same single connection every time, and that connection must be allowed to cross threads.

Specific: create_engine("sqlite://", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}, poolclass=StaticPool). Then create the tables on it. Build the app with create_app(engine) instead of importing app. Each fixture that opens something yields it and cleans up after the yield.

Implementation: engine creates the engine, calls Base.metadata.create_all(...), yields it and disposes it afterwards. db is `with Session(engine) as session:` with a yield inside. client is `with TestClient(create_app(engine)) as c:` with a yield inside. Import Base and create_app from app, and StaticPool from sqlalchemy.pool.
evaluation: A new engine and new tables for each test (function scope)
Every fixture cleans up after yield
You can explain both failure modes: 'no such table' without StaticPool, and the thread error without check_same_thread=False
